title: The Star That Moved Wrong
plot_function: Establish ritual order and the generational contrast between Nari’s youthful curiosity and Orem’s accumulated trust in established truths. Nari carefully verifies the seventh-star anomaly because she fears being wrong; Orem suppresses the warning from experience and fear rather than ignorance. End with a repeatable lower-temple correspondence that gives Nari reason to investigate.

title: Beneath the God-Stone
plot_function: Reward and punish Nari’s curiosity. Her forbidden descent establishes repeatable correspondences between the wrong-moving star, the God-Stone, and the lower chamber, proving the inherited model incomplete without providing a replacement explanation. The encounter should deepen both her evidence and her fear, beginning to show her why Orem became cautious.

title: The Answering Light
plot_function: Bring Orem’s fear and Nari’s curiosity into direct confrontation without resolving the tension in favor of either. Orem confronts remorse over knowledge fear may have kept him from pursuing; Nari confronts the possibility that curiosity can reveal things whose consequences exceed human understanding and may have been safer left unknown. Neither reaches the wiser balance between curiosity and fear. The answering light follows a completed observed pattern and leaves both with more evidence but no ultimate explanation.
